asIsSteps.name: Load kegs on the delivery run
Work out rental fees by hand

sources.text: Every dispatch note lists the kegs loaded. Kegs stay the brewery's property while at a pub and must be traceable to that pub until they are collected. Drivers collect empties on the next delivery run.
A pub keeping a keg for more than 60 days is charged a monthly rental fee. Fees are worked out by hand from a spreadsheet at month end. Any fee waiver must be approved by the head of logistics.
The warehouse lead recounts the yard every Friday and corrects the keg spreadsheet.

outline.processName: Keg loan: dispatch, pick-up and rental settlement

steps.title: Ship kegs with the order into the pub's returnable stock
steps.purpose: Hold every dispatched keg against the pub that has it, still owned by the brewery.

steps.title: Record the pick-up and settle rental after the free period
steps.purpose: Return collected kegs to plant stock and charge monthly rental on kegs kept beyond the free period.

eliminatedAsIsSteps.reason: The pub-level stock balance replaces the Friday recount; only differences to the yard count are investigated.

coverage.rationale: Dispatch posts kegs to the pub's balance and the pick-up posts them back, so a keg is never untraced between the two.
Rental is settled monthly after the free period; the day the 60 days start from is held on EX-OQ-1.
A waiver request waits in an approval workflow; the fee changes only after the head of logistics approves it.

openQuestions.question: Do the 60 days start at goods issue or at delivery to the pub?

EX-1.trigger: A confirmed sales order containing beer and keg lines is released for delivery.
inputDocuments: Sales order with one keg line per keg size
outputDocuments: Outbound delivery referencing the sales order
Posted goods issue moving kegs to the pub's returnable stock

actions.operation: Add a keg line per size under the beer line and confirm the ship-to pub.
Create the outbound delivery, pick the kegs by batch and post goods issue.
Hold the issued quantity in the pub's returnable stock; the dispatch note prints from the delivery.

businessRules.condition: A keg line is on the delivery
businessRules.response: Post it to the pub's returnable stock; it is not invoiced and ownership does not pass.
Deliver what is available and leave the rest open on the order; never post negative stock.

exceptions.condition: The driver loads fewer kegs than the delivery lists
exceptions.response: Correct the delivery quantity before goods issue; the shortfall stays open on the order.

exceptions.condition: Goods issue was posted to the wrong pub
exceptions.response: Reverse it and repost to the right pub the same day, then tell the driver.

effects.inventory: Kegs move from plant stock to the pub's returnable stock, held per pub at plant level.
effects.financial: No revenue and no invoice for kegs; they stay in company valuation. Only beer lines are billed.
effects.ownership: The brewery keeps ownership; only custody passes to the pub until collection.

implementation.detail: Ship kegs by ordinary sales order into special stock indicator V (customer returnable packaging stock), as in S4-2023-INV-CUSTOMER-RETURNABLE-PACKAGING; the shipment is not billed. Validation points: serial-level tracking of a single keg is not evidenced, so tracking is by pub, quantity and batch; the stock landing is taken from the special stock definition and must be checked in the fit-to-standard workshop.

EX-1.addedValue: Every keg quantity sits against a named pub from the moment of dispatch, which replaces the Friday recount with a stock balance per pub.

acceptanceTests.given: An order for 20 beer kegs to pub P with 20 keg lines, and 25 kegs in unrestricted stock
acceptanceTests.when: The clerk posts goods issue for the delivery
acceptanceTests.then: Pub P's returnable stock shows 20 kegs, unrestricted stock falls to 5, and no invoice line exists for the kegs.

acceptanceTests.given: The driver loaded 18 of the 20 listed kegs
acceptanceTests.when: The clerk sets the delivery to 18 and posts goods issue
acceptanceTests.then: Pub P holds 18 kegs and the order keeps 2 open for the next run.

EX-2.trigger: A driver returns from a collection run with empty kegs from one or more pubs.
outputDocuments: Pick-up posting moving kegs from the pub's stock to plant stock
Interim or final rental settlement request

actions.operation: Post each pub's collected quantity back to plant stock against that pub.
Run the monthly rental settlement and review the credit and debit memo requests before release.

businessRules.condition: A keg has been with a pub beyond the free period
businessRules.response: Calculate the monthly fee as a percentage of keg value; the start of the period is held on EX-OQ-1.

businessRules.condition: Collected quantity is above the pub's balance
businessRules.response: Post only the balance and raise the difference to the dispatch supervisor.

businessRules.condition: A billing clerk asks to waive a fee
businessRules.response: Route the waiver to the head of logistics; the fee does not change until it is approved.

exceptions.condition: A fee request was created before a late pick-up was posted
exceptions.response: Delete the calculated fee before cancelling the request, then settle again.

fields: sales value used as the fee base

effects.inventory: Collected kegs move from the pub's stock back to plant stock.
effects.financial: Rental fees are billed per pub; kegs stay in company valuation.
effects.ownership: No change: the brewery owns the kegs throughout.

implementation.detail: Use returnable packaging settlement with a rental-free time, as in S4-2023-SD-RP-RENTAL-FEES. Validation points: the fee is a percentage of keg value, not a flat monthly rate; the final settlement can generate a credit memo once 100% of value is paid, which must be switched off; whether the 60 days start at goods issue or delivery is open (EX-OQ-1).

EX-2.addedValue: Fees come from posted dispatch and pick-up dates instead of a month-end spreadsheet, so a pub is charged only for kegs it still holds.

acceptanceTests.given: Pub P holds 20 kegs and returns 12 after the free period
acceptanceTests.when: The clerk posts the pick-up and runs the monthly settlement
acceptanceTests.then: Pub P's balance is 8, plant stock rises by 12, and the fee request covers only the days each keg was held.

acceptanceTests.given: The free-period start date is not yet decided
acceptanceTests.then: The fee requests stay under billing block until EX-OQ-1 is answered.

acceptanceTests.given: A fee of 120 is waived at the pub's request
acceptanceTests.when: The billing clerk submits the waiver
acceptanceTests.then: The fee stays 120 until the head of logistics approves, and then it is set to 0.

keyDesignDecisions.topic: Track kegs by quantity per pub or by serial number per keg

options.name: Quantity and batch per pub
options.pros: Standard stock; no scanning at dispatch.
options.cons: Cannot say which single keg is missing.

options.name: Serial number per keg
options.pros: Gives each keg its own history.
options.cons: Scan on every dispatch and pick-up; serial tracking in returnable stock is not evidenced.

keyDesignDecisions.rationale: R-1 asks for traceability to a pub, not to a single keg, so the standard option meets it. Revisit if the unaccounted-keg KPI does not fall.

fitGap.justification: Returnable packaging stock holds company-owned kegs per pub, so no custom object is needed.
Settlement with a rental-free time is customising, not delivered as is; a flat fee per keg would need an extension.
fitGap.validationReason: The fee is a percentage of keg value; confirm that is acceptable to the business.

masterDataPrerequisites.creationChannel: Created by the steward in the material master app; the keg register is loaded once at cutover.
masterDataPrerequisites.governance: Changes to the fee base or batch settings need the steward's approval and are logged.

dataMigration.source: Keg register spreadsheet after a Friday recount
dataMigration.approach: Cleanse to one row per pub and keg size, load as opening returnable stock, reconcile to the recount.
dataMigration.risk: Spreadsheet and yard counts disagree; freeze dispatch during the load.

cutover.activity: Freeze dispatch, load pub balances, reconcile to the recount, release dispatch.
cutover.risk: Kegs dispatched during the freeze are missed; log them on paper and key them after go-live.

interfaces.triggerFrequency: After each collection run, about daily
interfaces.payload: Pubs visited and kegs collected per pub
interfaces.validationReason: The released customer-return interface carries returns; confirm one exists for pick-ups from returnable stock.

failureHandling.detection: A pick-up the app sent and SAP rejected shows in the interface error list.
failureHandling.alerting: The dispatch supervisor gets a mail for every rejected pick-up.
failureHandling.rerun: The supervisor corrects the pub or batch and resends that pick-up only.
failureHandling.idempotency: The app's pick-up number is stored on the posting; a repeat is ignored.

kpis.name: Kegs unaccounted for at month end (count of kegs, per calendar month)
kpis.measuredFrom: Stock overview of returnable stock per pub, compared with the month-end yard count

objectives.statement: Know which pub holds every keg until it is collected.
objectives.measure: Kegs unaccounted for: fewer than 10 kegs a month

objectives.statement: Charge rental only for kegs a pub still holds after the free period.

scopeStatements.statement: Keg dispatch, pick-up and monthly rental settlement for pubs.
scopeStatements.reason: These are the three current steps in the ops notes.
The route-planning app stays and only sends pick-ups to SAP.

orgStructure.proposal: Use the one brewery plant for shipping; returnable stock is held per pub at plant level.
One storage location in the plant for kegs returned from pubs.
orgStructure.openPoint: Whether returned kegs need a location apart from clean stock is not decided.

reports.name: Kegs held per pub
reports.purpose: Show each pub's keg balance and days held so the dispatch supervisor can chase long holds.
reports.realization: Stock overview of returnable stock per pub.

endToEndTests.when: Dispatch, pick-up and the monthly settlement run in order
endToEndTests.then: The pub holds 8, plant stock rose by 12, and rental is charged only for the days held.
